instruction: Switch to the Outline view in LibreOffice Impress.

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(5); pyautogui.press('esc'); time.sleep(0.3); pyautogui.press('f10'); time.sleep(0.3); pyautogui.press('right', presses=2, interval=0.1); time.sleep(0.3); pyautogui.press('down', presses=11, interval=0.1); pyautogui.press('enter')

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully restored the hidden left slide panel by navigating View menu and clicking 'Slide Pane'. Completed in 5 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate View menu in LibreOffice Impress, identify and toggle UI panel visibility options, understand Impress layout panels
metadata.task_rationale: Model demonstrated proficiency with the View menu. Switching to Outline view (View > Outline) is a slightly harder variation because it changes the entire editing mode, not just a panel toggle. Tests deeper understanding of Impress view modes.
metadata.explanation: Task requires switching to Outline view via View > Outline. The evaluator uses partial credit: 0.5 for 'Outline' appearing in the accessibility tree, and 0.5 for the absence of Normal view placeholders ('Click to add Title'/'Click to add Text'). Returns combined score capped at 1.0.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (accessibility_tree) correctly extracts the UI state needed to determine the current Impress view mode.

Metric logic is semantically sound: checking for 'Outline'/'outline' in the accessibility tree and verifying absence of Normal view placeholders ('Click to add Title'/'Click to add Text') is a reasonable heuristic for detecting Outline view.
Partial credit scoring (0.5 + 0.5) is well-structured: presence of outline indicator + absence of normal view indicators provides robustness against false positives.
The 'expected' parameter ({'expected_view': 'outline'}) is passed to the metric but never used — all checks are hardcoded. This is functionally correct for this specific task but reduces reusability.

Minor false positive risk: the word 'Outline' could appear in accessibility tree menu items even when not in Outline view, but the dual-check approach mitigates this (would only yield 0.5 score in that case).
Single-step instruction ('Switch to Outline view') is fully covered by the evaluator.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using the 'expected' parameter (expected.get('expected_view')) to parameterize the view name check instead of hardcoding, improving reusability for other view mode checks.
Consider adding more outline-specific accessibility tree indicators (e.g., checking for outline-mode-specific widget names) to reduce false positive risk from menu items containing 'Outline'.
